evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 752: meō perīclō rem gerō
Cic. Rosc. Am. 110: perīculum adīre capitis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: At your own risk: tuō perīculō (Traupman 107, 371). To run a risk: perīculum adīre or subīre; Traupman’s perīculum facere is in Plautus (Lewis & Short), though more often it means “make trial of”. In danger: in perīculō esse. Risky: perīculōsus (Cato Agr. praef. 1), anceps (Traupman 372).

terms.gloss: a critical risk, a decisive moment
evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 12: in perīculum ac discrīmen vocātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To put at risk: in discrīmen vocāre.

evidence: Hor. C. 2.1.6: perīculōsae plēnum opus āleae

terms.gloss: risk, put at risk; put to the test
evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.11: salūs summa perīclitanda reī pūblicae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to put in peril, endanger, risk (rare but class.)”; more often “try, test”.
In this sense chiefly post-Augustan, above all in Tacitus; never so in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: mea fīdūciā opus condūxī et meō perīclō rem gerō
phrases.english: I’ve taken on the job on my own credit, and I’m running it at my own risk

phrases.latin: perīculōsae plēnum opus āleae tractās et incēdis per ignīs suppositōs cinerī dolōsō
phrases.english: you are handling a work full of dangerous risk, and walking over fires hidden under treacherous ash

phrases.latin: Caret perīclō, quī etiam cum est tūtus cavet.
phrases.english: He runs no risk who takes care even when he is safe.
to run the risk of one’s life
